db.functional_unit: 1 m2 of external wall, 12 mm cement plaster on both faces unless stated, conductivities in the dry state (moisture effects not modelled)

policy.missing_value_policy: A missing value is never imputed. A material is ranked only if the weight of criteria that have a value at or above min_grade is at least min_completeness. Scores use only available criteria with weights renormalised, and are labelled partial.

grades.B: recognised published dataset or peer-reviewed study (check geography)
grades.C: generic industry average, aggregator record, secondary report or estimate - provisional
grades.D: missing / unsupported - never contributes to a ranking

statuses.read_primary: value taken from a primary document that was opened and read
statuses.secondary_reported: value reported by an unverified secondary summary; check the primary document
statuses.derived: calculated by this platform from cited inputs

criteria.name: Wall U-value (calculated, ENS 2024 method)
criteria.rationale: Conductive heat gain through the wall; ENS 2024 prescribes this calculation method (Sec. 9.3).

criteria.name: Embodied carbon, masonry core only (A1-A3 where stated)
criteria.rationale: Core-layer GWP per m2 = factor x density x thickness. Excludes mortar, plaster, transport, replacement. Boundaries differ between sources.

criteria.name: Masonry unit cost (INR/m2 of wall face, units only)
criteria.rationale: Redefined in v3 to the part that can be evidenced from public price listings: unit price x pieces per m2. Excludes mortar, plaster, labour, transport, wastage. Full installed cost still needs dealer quotations.

criteria.name: Expected service life
criteria.rationale: Requires published or manufacturer evidence with basis.

criteria.name: Maintenance demand
criteria.rationale: Requires expert judgement or inspection evidence.

candidates.name: Laterite stone blocks
candidates.kerala_relevance: Kerala-native quarried stone; long vernacular use, strong regional identity.

assembly.note: Core thickness is a placeholder. ENS Table 46 has no laterite entry; U-value cannot be calculated until a cited conductivity exists.

core_density.note: Quarry-specific; measure per IS 9620 (S08) test report.

gwp.note: No cited LCA/EPD. Quarried, unfired - low carbon is plausible but UNPROVEN.

candidate_unverified.note: Reported by an unidentified Malabar study; excluded from all calculations.

rating_notes: GRIHA 19.1.3 lists 'Stones from India (not including stone cladding)' - whether quarried laterite blocks qualify must be confirmed with GRIHA.

reported_notes.text: Kozhikode lateritic soil blocks: 8% cement by soil weight reported optimum; strength and density rise, water absorption falls with cement. No conductivity reported. Search summary only.

gwp.basis: Auroville Earth Institute, 'country fired bricks', India (Auroville/Pondicherry), 2005. Page states 'Kg of CO2', not CO2e; modules not stated. Same source and basis as the CSEB figure.

alternative.note: Evora paper Table 1, ceramic block: ICE 2011 (UK) 0.22, Portugal 0.112 and 0.100, UM 0.19. At 1920 kg/m3 x 230 mm this gives 44-97 kgCO2/m2 versus 147.9 from Auroville.

masonry_unit.note: Kochi, red clay brick 9x4x3 in, modelled estimate; 10 mm mortar joints assumed; 230 mm wall = two stretcher wythes.

candidates.name: AAC (autoclaved aerated concrete) blocks
candidates.kerala_relevance: Established Indian market; growing Kerala use (supplier evidence not yet collected).

gwp.basis: UK average AAC (61% pfa) from an APA/British Precast EPD via Climatiq; GWP method and lifecycle modules not stated by aggregator; not an Indian product.

masonry_unit.note: Kochi, 600x200x200 mm block, modelled retail estimate (dealer range reported as Rs 64-102). Thin-bed joint assumed 0 mm; 200 mm wall = one block thick.

rating_notes: GRIHA 19.1.3 accepts AAC blocks only with at least 40% fly ash content by weight (or a valid GRIHA Product Catalogue certificate, 19.2.10).

candidates.name: Compressed stabilised earth block (CSEB)
candidates.kerala_relevance: Auroville/Indian sustainable-construction practice; niche uptake in Kerala.

assembly.note: ENS Table 46 value used (1.201 W/mK at 1800 kg/m3). Auroville's own table gives 0.81-0.93 W/mK, which would give U about 2.1-2.2 W/m2K instead of 2.53.

gwp.basis: Auroville hand-press CSEB, 5% cement, 2005 (India). Page also shows 51.5 kg/m3 in a second table; unit kg CO2, modules not stated.

rating_notes: GRIHA 19.1.3 lists adobe / stabilised adobe / CSEB / stabilised mud blocks as alternative wall materials.

candidates.name: Hollow concrete blocks

layers.label: Hollow concrete block core (no cited conductivity)

assembly.note: ENS Table 46 lists SOLID concrete blocks only. Hollow-block conductivity depends on voids; use a product test report, or ENS Eq. 2 (k = 0.1009 exp(0.0011 rho), valid 600-2100 kg/m3) if measured dry density is available.

gwp.note: Cement content drives GWP; need product EPD or mix design.

masonry_unit.note: Thiruvananthapuram, 400x200x200 mm hollow concrete block, modelled estimate. No cited conductivity yet, so no U-value.

rating_notes: GRIHA 19.1.3 accepts hollow concrete blocks only with at least 40% fly ash content by weight.

legacy_indicative._note: Original prototype values, all verified=false, kept only for the 'legacy parity' demo. Do not treat as findings. Note: legacy U-values differ from ENS-method calculations (e.g. CSEB 1.60 legacy vs calculated value).

thermal_dynamic.note: EN ISO 13786 periodic heat-transfer matrices; indicators only - NOT scored (see S14 double-counting warning). Uses Table 46 specific heat.

retv.locator: Sec. 9.5.2 and Table 48 (warm-humid); omega: Table 49 (lat < 23.5 N)
retv.formula_note: RETV = (1/A_envelope) [ a*sum(A_op*U_op*w) + b*sum(A_win*U_win*w) + c*sum(A_win*SHGC_eq*w) ]. Eq. 4 is an image in the ENS PDF; the form here follows the variable list printed beneath it (Sec. 9.5.3) and must be checked against the printed equation.

items.requirement: RETV of the building envelope (except roof) <= 15 W/m2 for composite, hot-dry, warm-humid and temperate zones. BEE notes an intended future tightening to 12 W/m2.
items.applies_to: whole envelope (walls + openings), not a single wall material

items.requirement: Warm-humid RETV formula coefficients a=5.15, b=1.31, c=65.21 (formula itself, Eq. 4, not transcribed here).
Wall U-value = 1/(Rsi + sum(t/k) + Rse) with Rsi=0.13, Rse=0.04 m2K/W; Table 46 gives default conductivities; measured values per IS codes may replace them.
k = 0.0652 exp(0.0012 rho) for solid fired clay brick (1250-2150 kg/m3); k = 0.1009 exp(0.0011 rho) for non-fired units incl. AAC, concrete block, fly ash brick, CSEB (600-2100 kg/m3).
items.applies_to: masonry units with measured dry density

items.requirement: Kochi and Trivandrum are classified Warm-Humid. Kollam is not listed in the extracted table; adjacent-city classification is an inference.

All internal and external walls built from alternative materials: concrete blocks (hollow, solid or AAC) with >=40% fly ash by weight; hollow clay blocks; adobe/stabilised adobe/CSEB/stabilised mud blocks; rammed earth; stones from India (not cladding); bamboo/rapidly renewable material; monolithic concrete wall with >=20% OPC replacement; C&D waste blocks with >=30% C&D waste; dry walls/boards with >=5% recycled content. Evidence: purchase orders, BOQ, mix design or valid GRIHA Product Catalogue certificate (19.2.8-19.2.13).
>=30% replacement of OPC with BIS-recommended waste by weight in masonry mortar and plaster.

GWP reduction vs a project-specific GRIHA LCA base case: superstructure 10-15% = 1 point, >15% = 2 points; interiors and finishes 10-15% = 1, 15-30% = 2, >30% = 3. Needs a third-party LCA calculator report, EPDs or GRIHA Product Catalogue certificates.

Thermal comfort by simulation (NBC 2016 / ASHRAE 55 / Indian Adaptive Comfort): non-AC spaces 60% of occupied hours in warm-humid climate (90% elsewhere), or Alternative 2 natural-ventilation strategies.
Recycled-content materials at 10% and 20% thresholds (2 points) as reported by a search summary of the addendum.
